messages:
maya: quick sync — followup to the rate-limiter RFC. thinking about a lightweight handshake between frontdoor and admission so we can smooth bursts while folding in abuse signals. thoughts?

trent: sg. can you sketch the minimal signals we need? admission decision, provisional tokens, and abuse_score?

maya: yep — three things: 1) decision: admit/queue/drop with a reason code; 2) provisional_tokens: tiny allotment to let probes through and measure intent; 3) abuse_score: 0..1 float that modulates penalties and token scaling.

liam: how long do provisional tokens live? we should avoid long-lived leaky buckets that attackers can game.

maya: short TTL by default — like 10s. refill only on steady consumption. sketch: ```proto
message Handshake {
  string tenant = 1;
  int32 provisional_tokens = 2;
  int32 ttl_secs = 3;
  float abuse_score = 4;
  string reason = 5; // optional reason code
}
```

ev an: we also need fairness constraints. provisional tokens must be scaled by historical baseline and a per-tenant cap so noisy tenants can't hog the queue.

trent: +1. frontdoor should include route hints (model_id, seq_len_category, priority) so admission can pick the right policy and kernel-class.

maya: policy idea: provisional = floor(min(burst_cap, baseline_rate * window_factor)) then clamp to per-model caps. if abuse_score > 0.6 => reduce provisional by factor.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout scheduled for handshake feature flag on cluster-alpha 0->5% at 03:00 UTC.

liam: edge case: attackers opening many short-lived connections. we need client-level soft probation (probation window 60s) and exponential backoff for repeated probes. tie probation to ephemeral client_id + ip heuristics.

maya: agreed. also add a short probation that disables provisional tokens for repeat offenders and escalates to heavier penalties if abuse persists.

ev an: telemetry requirements: emit provisional_granted, provisional_consumed, probe_rejected, abuse_score_histogram, and a probe_latency metric. need A/B to measure latency vs token cost.

trent: operationally: implement handshake protobuf, add admission endpoint POST /v1/handshake that returns the Handshake proto. frontdoor adds header X-RW-Handshake:1 and fallback header X-RW-Handshake-Status when handshake fails. start RFC addendum + small canary next week. anyone object?

evan: no objections. add fallback behavior: if handshake times out, frontdoor should default to conservative admission (queue with very low slots) to avoid opening up attack surface.

liam: :thumbsup: i'll open a PR for protobuf schema, unit tests, and a simple simulator to validate fairness impact.

maya: thanks — i'll author the RFC addendum and add a short experiment plan (metrics to watch + rollback thresholds). linking it here once done.
